Source 95f421513ee961a1 §2, (2), and the vertical-plane paragraph give the same projective construction and constants, within the source's convex-body setting.

For a convex D the positive-denominator projective map preserves segments and has the inverse b↦b/(1+k·b) on the image, so the base and the projective graph cover the whole sections as claimed. The ray parameter 2(1−k·x)/3 is strictly between zero and one under both stated bounds.

The graph-area factor yields S/||(-3k,1)||=4|D|/9, and the apex margin two gives pyramid volume 8|D|/27. Horizontal slices have volume element 3t²|B| dt; the total is |B| and mean t is 3/4. The raw centroid margin is −(1+9k·g_B)/4, yielding the displayed scalar.

The centered base chord and the apex give a triangular section with centroid zero. Homothetic horizontal sections preserve the planar cap fraction. The section-area multiplier 3/2 and centroid projection multiplier 3/4 give the scalar factor 9/8. At D=[−1,1]^2, k=(1/4,0), exact area and centroid are |B|=1024/225 and g_B=(16/45,0), giving p=25/96 and s=−45/256.

Under the revised hypothesis the segment-preserving projective map and its segment-preserving inverse b↦b/(1+k·b) show that B is convex and that the rational vertex set is carried bijectively onto the vertex set of B. Thus the stated convex hull K has actual base B, and at least four base vertices give at least five total vertices.

The former nonconvex reading permitted the rational cross with |D|=12 and |conv D|=14 at k=0, so the original volume formula could fail. Convexity removes exactly that defect, with all permitted k and both oblique and centered vertical calculations intact.

issues.defect: An arbitrary rational polygon need not be convex. Its projective image then need not be convex, while the specified K has convex hull of B as its base. The rational cross witness in checks contradicts |K|=|B|.
issues.locator: Statement opening and proof first paragraph, from segment preservation to a convex base
issues.repair: Add convex to the hypothesis on D. The section and volume proof then uses the actual projective base.

overlap.comparison: Uses a centrally symmetric base and a truncated projective chart. It does not provide the nonsymmetric base obtained by projectively mapping a centroid-zero polygon.
